pitch_detail.notes: Starts at the foot of the Root Canal gully. Climb the right-hand (north) wall of the gully by a right-facing corner that sits left of the bolted face, then top out on a ledge and belay in the wall above.

Move the belay right to the base of the broad snowy weakness and follow its center upward until you reach the right-hand end of the following short vertical step. At least 70 m of climbing, so it stretches the rope; some teams simul-climb it or split it in two.

review.changed: Wrote both pitches. P2 length is stated as 70+ m so it is in the notes, not lengthM. The continuation above (Bathos/Root Canal) is not described pitch by pitch and was left out. No rappel table (descent is a 3rd/4th class walk-off).

pitch_detail.anchor: fixed lost arrow piton plus knifeblade and small gear
pitch_detail.notes: From the start, a short corner on the left side leads up and right into the chimney proper, which you follow through a couple of steeper bits to its top. Step left onto the ledge, then work up and left to a belay under another corner, set at a fixed lost arrow piton; a knifeblade and small gear back it up.

Step back to the right and take the next corner, which is in darker rock, and avoid both the corner directly above the belay and the looser chimney further right. The darker rock is still loose, so clean as you go. Surmount the chimney into the snow gully and belay just above a fixed knifeblade, which also keeps the rope from sweeping debris onto the follower.

Work up and left in the snow gully, keeping a big solitary conifer on your left, and carry on to the ridge crest. Moderate to steep snow with short 5th class steps and plenty of belay options; roughly 300 ft (about 90 m); the whole stretch from the P2 belay to the crest can be moved together.

review.changed: Wrote 3 pitches; no pitch grades are given so none written. P3 length is approximate so it is in the notes. No rappel table (walk-off descent).

pitch_detail.notes: Follow a long corner system up to a roof in off-fingers size, then belay on a good ledge a little above it.
Climb a crack in the face, step right, and continue thin to wide hands. The belay is a single bolt backed up with a small stopper.
Climb left from the belay, aiming for the left-hand crack system that splits the headwall. Going too far left puts you in the main wide-crack corner, too far right in a loose chimney.

review.changed: Wrote 3 pitches with the stated grades; no lengths given. No rappels described.

pitch_detail.notes: A variation that leaves Storm Mountain Falls above the second-pitch anchors. Keep angling left past a few bulges, on the thin ice just left of the catcher's mitt formation, to a gear anchor above the overhang of the 5.8 route to the left. The pitch is rated M3-4.

pitch_detail.anchor: chains at top of the 5.8 route
pitch_detail.notes: Tight and awkward. Drytool into the corner and ramp holding the obvious ice flow on the left edge of the overhung mitt formation; swing room is minimal and the ice is thin. It leads into a tight mixed corner choked with ice, and the belay is on the chains atop the neighboring 5.8 route.

review.changed: Only pitches 3 and 4 are described (pitches 1-2 are the base route); wrote those two with their stated labels. Stored count 4 not padded.

pitch_detail.notes: Blocky ground with a few pins leads into the corner, then the chimney to its left reaches loose terrain. Belay at a two-bolt anchor above the ledge on your left. Overhead avalanche exposure from the start zone high above, and rockfall.
Cross a snow ramp to the right, heading for the left-facing corner at the heart of the gully. A few M3 moves lead into the main gully, where a two-bolt anchor sits on an outcrop in its center.
Go straight up the gully, hugging the left side to reduce overhead hazard, to an outcrop anchor with a pin and a bolt.

Pass the outcrop on its left side and traverse over a second gully, crossing a couple of short rock steps if snow has not buried them, to another outcrop with a two-bolt anchor. An alternative goes right of the P3 belay and up a faint rib.

pitch_detail.anchor: 2 bolts (right variant) or built on blocky ledges (left variant)
pitch_detail.notes: Two variants. Left: from the bolts traverse into another snow gully that steepens, follow it until it opens onto the snowfield below the spire (about 140 m of steep, serious snow; simul-climb, a fall here would be bad), and head toward the spire trending slightly right. Do not belay at the two bolts on the left at the rock; build an anchor 20-30 ft right on loose blocky ledges. Right: climb a loose rock band, about 70 m of M3, to a two-bolt anchor on a ledge about 15 m away. Either way, find those bolts, since they matter for the descent.

If you took the rock variant on P5, plod 70 m of 35 degree snow to the base of the spire. Build the belay on the loose blocky ledges right of the tower; the two-bolt anchor beneath the spire is exposed to rockfall and should be avoided. This pitch is also subject to wind loading.

Take the corners above the belay with great care, since the rock is very loose, then work across a chain of steps and ledges toward the spire, keeping as high as you can. A step over the gap between spire and wall lands on a ledge with a two-bolt anchor. Rockfall has damaged ropes here.

Climb the corner above past two bolts, and commit left onto the main face at the second bolt. Follow good rock past one bolt to the ledge under the summit block, traverse right past a bolt around the block, and climb the final chimney to the top. A purple totem may be handy.

review.changed: Wrote all 8 pitches. P5 has two variants with different lengths so no single lengthM. No rappel table: descent is 'rap the route, down climbing as necessary' with no station list. Route has objective avalanche and rockfall hazard, noted in pitches.
review.other_findings: Stored length 305 m is shorter than the summed pitch lengths (about 500 m).

pitch_detail.notes: Easy, smooth-stoned slab. Climb to the apex of the slab, top out, and sling a horn for the anchor.
A long stretch of 3rd class to another slab that is best soloed.
A short dihedral leads to bushes at the top. A horn sling makes a solid anchor.
From the belay at the top of P3, simul-climb or solo the ridgeline, linking slabs and some crumbly sections to the top of the formation and the gondola top station.

review.other_findings: Stored length 169 m vs about 180 m from pitch lengths; minor.

pitch_detail.notes: A slab of ice that forms reliably. Belay from a tree.
A short pitch up to a pine tree belay.
A short, steep curtain of ice at the top.

review.changed: Wrote 3 pitches (60 ft, 25 ft, 20 ft converted). Descent is a rappel from trees, no station list so no rappel table.

pitch_detail.notes: Rope up below the first small icicle, where hand-size gear in the roof makes a belay. Trend up and left through poor ice, then over overhanging rock steps. A little fixed tat sits on a ledge 20 ft left, or climb one more tier to a natural anchor. Watch rope drag.

pitch_detail.anchor: hex/beak/pin combination, back up with a cam
pitch_detail.notes: Head straight up from the natural belay, keeping left where the gear is good. The anchor is an old hex, beak and pin combination, so back it up with a 0.75 cam.
Steeper than the first two. A few short roofs alternate between thin ice and mixed ground, followed by steep snow to a belay below a roof that has a grubby, dripping offwidth. Pin anchor.

Open route-finding. One line traverses hard right across the amphitheater over snow and short vertical terraces to a big blocky chimney/offwidth; avoid it without a deep freeze, since big blocks are frozen in. Above the huge detached block is one hard, exposed move to a tree belay.

Get to the middle of the amphitheater via sloping snow shelves; this is where the best ice of the route is. Clip the slung pine halfway up, then finish through a little scratching and mixed snow-ice and more rock to the long snow slope above, which could count as two more pitches.

review.changed: Wrote 5 pitches. Descent is a long walk-off with one rappel; no station list so no rappel table.
review.other_findings: Stored length 183 m vs about 235 m from pitch lengths.

pitch_detail.notes: Cracks lead up the face with very little protection; only about three pieces for the whole pitch, so it is serious despite the easy grade. Use the full rope past a doubtful knifeblade and a lost arrow on a ledge (two old pins), then climb the dihedral about 10 ft more to a belay at a slung horn and a #1 cam crack.

Leave the belay and keep following the dihedral to a mossy crack on the face. It reaches a roof with a solid #3.5 placement; get past the roof on its right side, and go left along a ledge about 20 ft to a flake belay.
A cleaner variation may exist, so look around. The known line heads left into a dirt-filled, chossy chimney, then some 4th class ground, to a big tree for the belay; roughly 55 m.

review.changed: Wrote 3 pitches; P3 length is approximate so it is in the notes.
review.other_findings: Stored length 152 m is shorter than about 176 m from pitch lengths.

pitch_detail.notes: A boulder-problem start with a hanging mantle gains a ledgy stance and a high first bolt, the only bolt on the route. Cracks continue straight up to a big piece in the roof; pull over onto a technical face, and mantle to a two-bolt belay on a large ledge. Skip the sandy 5.7 funnel on the right.

Jams and laybacks reach the corner above. Go straight up and move carefully around the loose block below the roof, without placing gear in the crack behind it. Establish under the .5 crack through the center of the roof and crank through on finger locks and small gritty holds. Above, easier ground wanders left about 50 ft to a two-bolt anchor under the big flake.

A huge vertical flake that steepens as you climb. Climb some loose ground and a small corner to a stance and bush that guard its start. The flake begins wide, narrows with blind gear, and gets more strenuous; smear, stem and lieback up and out left at the chossy roof to a two-bolt anchor.
Wandery and loose at first. Go up to the big blocky ledge, work right to a corner crack that takes gear, and pull a thin crux to a short hand crack and a two-bolt belay at a hanging block.

The easiest pitch, but worth doing. Thrash up the tree-covered ledge past a rappel anchor toward the obvious splitter on the summit tower, and jam to a belay on a ledge beneath the top, out left. Length is given as 40 m or more.

review.changed: Wrote 5 pitches. Descent is 6 rappels on a 60 m rope (including the station above the trees passed on P5), but no per-station detail, so no rappel table.

pitch_detail.notes: Begin on the pedestal next to a bolt and climb up and a little left, using cams in the horizontal breaks, to a slab with a second bolt. Clip it, pull the roof, and mantle onto a chossy ledge. Go left to a finger crack that seams out, make a boulder move, then work through a small dihedral and notch, scramble up the choss to the top of the short wall, and belay at a two-bolt anchor.
Scramble the loose slope, unroped or one climber at a time, to a rap anchor on the ledge that sits beneath the next wall.
Start up hand cracks and blocks 5-10 ft right of the anchor. Mix jams and face holds with compression through a few roofs to a pedestal with a two-bolt belay.

Move left from the belay on edges to a thin crack that becomes steep juggy blocks. A short easy but unprotectable face section leads to a ledge below a big dihedral. Climb it, stemming and mantling right at its end, tiptoe through loose ground to a chimney/arete, and climb that to the final anchor. A 70 m rope is needed.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel straight down the face to the top of pitch 2, not left into the dihedral; this line is clean and pulls easily.
An easy rappel down to the ledge anchor under pitch 2; the rope length needed is given as 30+ m.
Optional rap to the top of pitch 1, 30+ m. Skip it by walking down the loose slope instead. Pull slowly, since the rope can knock rocks onto you.
Rappel to the chossy pedestal and first bolt, not to the packs in the cave. Thread the rope through the larger notch, right of the small one used on the way up. Length is 35+ m.

review.changed: Wrote 3 numbered pitches plus the 1.5 scramble, and 4 rappels in the order described (rappel 3 optional); lengths other than 35 m are stated as 30+ or 35+ so they are in notes only.

pitch_detail.notes: Approach pitch. Steep stemming from the ground reaches a ledge (loose rock there), and a shorter, easier corner continues to the big midway ledge. Belay on gear, tips to fingers sizes.

The natural line up the middle of the buttress: a stem box to double cracks, a layback around a bulge, then straight-in jamming. A short fist section takes a #4, though a #3 placed deep works too. Two-bolt anchor.

Slot a 0.4 on the left right above the belay. Step right into a short right-facing corner, then tiptoe back left across a band of unappealing rock to a bolt over the roof, and pull hard. Steep cracks and face holds lead to a two-bolt anchor.

review.changed: Wrote 3 pitches. Descent is two single-rope rappels with a 70 m rope to the midway ledge, then a scramble; no station detail so no rappel table.

pitch_detail.notes: Approach pitch. Steep stemming from the ground reaches a ledge (loose rock there), and a shorter, easier corner continues to the big midway ledge. Belay on gear, tips to fingers sizes.
Stem box to double cracks, a layback around a bulge, and straight-in jamming. A #3 placed deep handles the short fist section. Two-bolt anchor.

Slot a 0.4 on the left right above the belay, step right into a short corner, tiptoe back left over poor rock, and clip the bolt above the roof. After you are established, back up your second, then go left to the arete: two bolts and a #2 cam in a pod cover it. A ledge, then a rightward trend, brings a finger-crack boulder problem and a two-bolt anchor.

review.changed: Wrote 3 pitches. Descent same as the neighboring routes (two single-rope rappels to the midway ledge); no station list so no rappel table.

pitch_detail.notes: Approach pitch. Steep stemming from the ground reaches a ledge (loose rock there), and a shorter, easier corner continues to the big midway ledge. Belay on gear, tips to fingers sizes.

Jam and stem the left-facing corner until about 20 ft below the big triangular roof, then angle right over the face and round the arete onto a ledge system that works as a foot traverse. A two-bolt anchor is there if you find the right line.

Traverse right from the belay to below a right-facing corner right of the roof. Layback and stem it, or escape onto the left face; steep face climbing on positive holds with good gear leads to the top.

review.changed: Wrote 3 pitches. Descent via rappels and scramble is not given station by station, so no rappel table.

pitch_detail.notes: Start up a chossy pillar below the large inverted cross on the column. Clip one bolt, reach intermittent cracks, and get solid gear in the center of the cross. Boulder up with the wide crack and face holds, mantle onto a small ledge, and climb the small corner above to a tiered ledge with a two-bolt anchor.

Head up and left into the big open book, and stem, crimp and jam to the corner top. Scramble 20-30 ft of 4th class to a shrubby chimney that climbs better than it looks, and belay at a nest-like stance where pitch 3 starts.

A consistent pitch of 30+ m (length given as a minimum). Start up the widening crack, angling slightly right through incipient cracks, horizontals and slab. Mantle onto the ledge under the big arete, continue right above or through a large shrub, and belay in a corner beneath a steep wide crack at a two-bolt anchor.

Follow the wide crack; at a large overhang, step right around the corner into a huge chimney filled with talus. Stay left, stemming and jamming, trending slightly left to the base of the huge roof. Exit through the right side with face and intermittent cracks, trending right around the arete with exposed moves to a ledge with a two-ring anchor. Bring plenty of alpine draws to limit drag.

review.changed: Wrote 4 pitches. Descent is 4 rappels with a 70 m rope but stations are not described, so no rappel table.

pitch_detail.notes: Start up a right-slanting corner; some mixed moves lead to thin ice on the left. Keep going up the ice until you can step left into a low-angle corner holding snow, where you belay.
Follow an ice runnel up to a cave holding fixed gear, and belay there. Descend by rappel; two single-rope rappels get you down.

review.changed: Wrote 2 pitches; no grades or lengths per pitch. Rappel count is stated but not as a station list, so no rappel table.

pitch_detail.notes: After easy snow through the trees and loose rock to the start of steeper snow, head left up the main gully to rappel anchors on the right.
Steeper snow leads to some easy low-angle ice. Exit the gully to the right to rappel anchors.

review.changed: Wrote 2 pitches. Fixed rappel anchors are mentioned (one set at the top, one a full 60 m rappel below) but not as an ordered station list, so no rappel table.
